Provigil, also called modafinil, is a drug that has been called "the secret to success", "the world's first safe smart-drug", and perhaps most interesting, "a real Limitless pill".

Hmm. It all sounded too good to be true. I'm a skeptical man, and decided more research was needed.

On the surface, modafinil is a wakefulness promoting agent. However, denizens of the internet have discovered other uses - as a cognition enhancer, antidepressant, treatment for chronic fatigue, and aphrodisiac. It's replaced Adderall for some. It's replaced opioids for others. Also, it's been approved for use on certain U.S. Air Force missions.

So, after making damn sure this stuff wouldn't kill me, I decided to take the plunge. I order a few hundred pills online and began experimenting with dosages for approx 3 months. This is an honest, no-bullshit review of what I experience on modafinil, and later armodafinil (a similar, more potent substance).

8:30am, the first morning: I took two pills, or 400MG, of modafinil-- two to four times the recommended dose. Full disclosure: I've been diagnosed with ADD and depression, and have chronic fatigue due to breathing problems. YMMV.

I sat at the computer and got a little more work done than usual the first hour, but didn't feel much of an effect. I would later discover that sometimes "no news is good news". It's a subtle drug. You might feel a little bit euphoric, or some side effects (which I'll get into) - but if not, no worries.

10:08am: I started to get aggravated, no patience. Little things that distracted me from the task at hand - in this case, working - pissed me off. However, the work I was doing was sporadic. It was nothing like Adderall, where I could focus on one thing for extended periods. I would write code, clean around the house, even exercise. I still felt ADD, but a more efficient ADD. No laziness.

12:29pm: Got back from a run, and started feeling weird. Sick. One minute I'd be too hot, then the next too cold. Spent a lot of time going back and forth messing with the AC. Still working on various projects during this time.

2:45pm: went with friends to town. I was still feeling impatient, but tried to not let it show. Lower back feels sore. I feel sluggish. A slight noticeable pressure in chest, but no arm tingling or other heart attack symptoms.

11:00pm: posted online, and went to bed at a reasonable hour. If I had to, I would describe my first day on modafinil as "wanting to go 100mph in a body that clocked out at 50mph."

Over the next few months, however, things changed.

Here's a breakdown of what I experienced:
â€¢ I can now take 300mg of armodafinil at night and stay up 50+ hours. I might still feel tired while doing so. But the "primal urge" to sleep is gone. I'm in control. I can "shake off" the desire to sleep, like it's nothing.
â€¢ Same with food. I can go a long time without eating. I also have to make sure I drink enough water, else I forget.
â€¢ I'm a little more paranoid than usual.
â€¢ It's not an Adderall replacement. Like I said, it's subtle. It's an anti-amphetamine - similar benefits, but with its own sort of side effects.
â€¢ My lower back will sometimes hurt, and I'll get muscle cramps - but I've contributed this to not drinking enough water.
â€¢ You can get "lost" in something such as work. I once spent 12+ hours on a video that I was going to post on YouTube, editing down to each individual frame, changing the littlest things, becoming more and more obsessed. Oh, and at the same time learning a completely new editing software. I didn't end up uploading the video.
â€¢ Libido goes through the roof.
â€¢ Emotions are much deeper, and colorful.
â€¢ I have different likes and dislikes. When I'm not on modafinil, I don't much care for hiphop. When I'm on it, it's all I listen to. The way I write is different. Even the porn I watch is different.
â€¢ Less depressed

I've also experienced a large number of the "traditional" side effects, including:
â€¢ minor hallucinations, after 40+ hours without sleep
â€¢ chest pain
â€¢ agitation
â€¢ nausea, diarrhea,
â€¢ insomnia
â€¢ abnormal vision - blurry vision in left eye
â€¢ odd smelling urine

IN CONCLUSION:
While not the "miracle drug" it's touted as, I've never been able to stay awake as long as I have while on Provigil. It also brought out a side of me I never knew existed, as corny as that sounds. However, I didn't get the superfocus, or brainfog-cleansing effects some users claim. I'll continue to use it, but in moderation.
Provigil: the truth behind the drug that's being touted as the "secret to success".
